subject: ACME POC: Evaluation plan, success criteria & eval methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC - post-call recap & proposed evaluation plan

Hi Jordan / Priya 

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed next step so we can get the POC scheduled: 

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: Validate Redwood's inference for ACME's customer support summarization flow (batch and live).
- Primary success metrics: accuracy of extracted action items, hallucination rate, latency under target traffic, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Data: sample of 10k support tickets (anonymized) to be used for offline tests; live shadow on 2 agents for online validation.

Proposed POC (2-week core phase + 2-week ramp)
- Week 0: Kickoff, access to sample data, security scoping, and SOW sign-off. Owner: ACME (Priya) + Redwood (Marissa).
- Weeks 1-2: Offline evals + model tuning. Deliverable: evaluation report, sample outputs. Owner: Redwood (Dylan)
- Weeks 3-4: Online shadow in non-customer-facing environment (or low-traffic routing) + user QA. Deliverable: production shadow report, rollback criteria. Owner: ACME eng + Redwood SRE

Success criteria (proposed, please confirm)
- Extraction accuracy: >= 92% F1 on action-item extraction (offline gold labels)
- Hallucination: < 5% severe hallucinations as measured by human review sample
- Latency: p95 < 450ms for 1k token contexts under simulated load (ACME target: 500ms)
- Cost: projected endpoint cost within ACME's target budget (Redwood will model)

Eval methodology options (we should align on this):
- Offline evals: run batch on labeled sample, compute metrics (precision/recall/F1), and run human rating for hallucination and relevance. Pros: deterministic, fast, repeatable. Cons: may miss emergent behaviors in live routing.
- Online shadow: mirror live traffic to Redwood endpoints with no customer impact, collect outputs and compare to current system / human labels. Pros: highest fidelity; Cons: requires slightly more ops coordination and safety controls.

Attached: draft POC evaluation plan (ACME_POC_eval_plan_v1.xlsx) and a first-pass rubric (POC_rubric_v1.md). Also attaching a draft SOW for legal review.

Please review and confirm:
1) Success criteria above (or propose edits)
2) Preferred eval approach (offline-only vs offline + shadow)
3) Any timeline constraints (we penciled mid-Apr start)

Thanks  happy to jump on a 20-min alignment if useful.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC - post-call recap & proposed evaluation plan

Thanks Marissa  this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Success criteria: the extraction F1 target is fine; can we change hallucination to be defined as "incorrect assertions about facts in the ticket that materially change the next action" and keep threshold at <5%? That wording will help our reviewers be consistent.
2) Eval approach: we prefer offline + online shadow. Offline to iterate quickly, shadow to validate in real traffic for ~3 days.
3) Timeline: mid-April start is OK but we need legal to review the SOW; can we aim for kickoff the week of Apr 12 if SOW signed by Apr 5?
4) Data access: we'll share anonymized 10k ticket sample by next Wednesday (31 Mar). Owner: Priya (I'll loop her).

Also, two asks: can you include a simple grading rubric for human raters (scale 1-5) covering relevance, completeness, and hallucination severity? And can we get an estimate of infra cost for 2 concurrent shadow agents for 3 days?

I'll get our legal and eng aligned and circle back.

Jordan
Product Lead, Conversational AI
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC - post-call recap & proposed evaluation plan

Appreciate the quick feedback, Jordan  that wording for hallucination is helpful, we'll adopt it in the rubric. A few updates based on your asks: 

- We've updated the attached rubric (POC_rubric_v1.md) to include a 1-5 human rating scale across:
  * Relevance (does the output address the requested action)
  * Completeness (are all necessary fields/actions captured)
  * Hallucination severity (1=no hallucination, 5=severe incorrect assertion)
  * Confidence/clarity (is response unambiguous)
  Weighting (suggested): Relevance 35%, Completeness 35%, Hallucination severity 25%, Latency/Throughput 5%

- Offline vs Shadow: Plan is to run 3 iterations of offline tests during Weeks 1-2. After we stabilize, we'll enable a 72-hour shadow (Weeks 3-4) for two agents with sampling at 10% to limit data volume. We'll provide scripts to anonymize outputs and a separate secure S3 drop for ACME's reviewers.

- Cost estimate for shadow (2 concurrent agents, 72 hours): preliminary estimate $1,200 total (GPU inference + data egress)  we'll refine after we know token distribution.

Next steps: 
1) Priya to confirm SOW timeline and share anonymized data by 2026-03-31.
2) ACME legal review SOW by 2026-04-05.
3) Redwood to finalize rubric & evaluation plan and share final POC package by 2026-04-07.

If useful I can set a 20-min alignment call early next week to walk the rubric and handoffs; otherwise I'll await Priya's data drop and legal note.

Thanks 
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
